messages:
alex: Heads-up 1 - spotted a telemetry/console mismatch: when an org-scoped API key is exchanged into a project context the trace UI shows only the project as the effective identity. That makes it difficult to map back to the originating org for billing and incident ownership.
maria: Can you paste repro steps and a minimal header dump so we can see where origin gets dropped?
alex: Repro: 1) create org API key, 2) call /v1/exchange -> get project token, 3) call /v1/generate with header `X-Redwood-Proxied-Project: proj-33`. In request detail UI the trace lists `effective_project=proj-33` but no origin. Example header dump:
```
Authorization: Bearer orgkey-acme-xxxx
X-Redwood-Proxied-Project: proj-33
X-Redwood-Origin: org:acme
X-Request-ID: req-abc123
```
sahil: We capture X-Redwood-Origin at ingress in raw logs. The console indexer canonicalizes identity into a single low-cardinality `effective_identity` column which overwrites origin when project is present. Proposed fix: add a separate low-cardinality `origin_org` tag.
kevin: Extra index tags increase write/storage cost in telemetry and we should be careful about exposing org names. Need RBAC gating to avoid leaking orgs to project viewers. Also consider hashing org ids in analytics.
maria: UX suggestion: keep `effective_identity` unchanged (avoid dashboard breakage). Show a subtle "origin" badge in the request detail pane when present, visible only to users with `read_org` permission. Add an `origin:<org>` filter option behind the same RBAC.
lucy: Product +1 for conservative rollout. Also propose an org-admin toggle to opt out of origin propagation if they want stricter isolation. Document in the changelog.
sahil: Implementation plan: 1) ingress: preserve X-Redwood-Origin into the request envelope metadata (no header mutation). 2) telemetry: emit `origin_org` as a forward-indexed low-cardinality string (no reindex of historical traces). 3) console: badge UI, filter, and RBAC checks. 4) auth: org opt-out enforced at token exchange time (strip origin if org disabled). Additionally emit a compact kinesis event for rollups.
kevin: For analytics, store a hashed_org = sha256(org_id) in metrics to avoid PII, while keeping readable org_name in console for users with permission. Need a cost estimate for the new index and retention implications.
maria: Rollout plan: feature flag `console.show_origin_in_traces` default OFF. Enable in staging for 2 weeks for eng-platform, collect metrics: fraction of traces with origin, filter usage, RBAC access attempts. Then enable internally and then opt-in external customers.
alex: Example compact kinesis event for devs:
{"event_type":"origin_hint","request_id":"req-abc123","origin_org":"acme","effective_project":"proj-33","ts":1835123600}
kevin: Ensure events are scrubbed for PII in analytics. For console views, enforce RBAC so only users with `read_org` see the readable org name.
sahil: Dev ownership: infra/ingress to preserve header + envelope, telemetry mapping and kinesis event (I'll own), console UI + RBAC (eng-platform), auth/org opt-out toggle (auth team). I'll open PRs for the mapping and event schema and share cardinality numbers by EOD.
lucy: I'll draft the internal rollout checklist and the short changelog copy for customers. Include an explanation of the org opt-out and privacy controls.
kevin: Add unit and integration tests for RBAC gating so origin badge/filter cannot be accessed by project-level viewers. We should also add a test for the org opt-out path to ensure stripping happens at exchange.
deploy-bot: feature flag `console.show_origin_in_traces` toggled ON in staging for team:eng-platform by lucy at 2026-03-22T10:12:03Z.
alex: Thanks all 1 - will watch telemetry and reopen if infra shows header loss. Closing for now, will link PRs when available. :wave:
